content.jointProblem: Can per-site unsupervised baselines and threshold calibration for ICS traffic be transferred to BACnet/IP and deployed on ArmaturaSec's embedded ProtoSense module to flag behavioural drift without labelled attacks? The first experiment would test whether such detectors can maintain operational false-alarm rates on held-out normal captures and controlled anomalies while producing explanations a plant manager can understand.

rationale.text: Kiss is open to joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions and to contract research on anomaly-detection deployment.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions
contract research on protocol traffic analysis and anomaly detection deployment

rationale.text: Kiss has built per-register statistical baselines and a one-class detector for Modbus/TCP traffic on a substation automation testbed.

sources.quote: per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed
one-class detector based on Mahalanobis distance thresholding over a 20-feature vector

rationale.text: She has worked on post-hoc threshold calibration using unlabelled operational data, which matches ArmaturaSec's need to set alert thresholds without attack labels.

sources.quote: post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data

rationale.text: Her work includes incremental online models for concept drift in ICS traffic, relevant to site-specific baseline drift and seasonal changes.

sources.quote: incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic without the need for periodic full retraining

rationale.text: She has evaluated lightweight detector deployment on ARM-class industrial gateways, relevant to ProtoSense's embedded inference constraints.

sources.quote: 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target

rationale.text: Her group operates an ICS testbed and long-term capture infrastructure that can support controlled experiments and validation.

sources.quote: dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection

rationale.text: She has experience with mixed-protocol and proprietary traffic, which is useful for extending detection beyond a single parsed protocol.

sources.quote: A one-class SVM and an Isolation Forest were trained on mixed-protocol captures

rationale.text: She prefers applied deployment collaborations rather than purely synthetic experiments, aligning with ArmaturaSec's operational product context.

sources.quote: prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments

constraints.text: The method must learn normal behaviour without confirmed malicious examples; ArmaturaSec has no confirmed attack captures and only normal traffic archives.

sources.quote: none of our clients has ever given us a packet capture that contains a confirmed attack
several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years

constraints.text: The detector must cover Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP, because ProtoSense is specified for both protocols.

sources.quote: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic

constraints.text: The collaboration must control false positives enough that clients do not disable alerts; a previous classifier was disabled in real deployments.

sources.quote: flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off

constraints.text: The detector must run on-device without affecting packet forwarding latency.

sources.quote: on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency

constraints.text: Alerts must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language.

sources.quote: explain to a plant manager in plain language

constraints.text: Company resources and IP access are limited to one to two part-time engineers and archives, bench and firmware codebase under NDA.

sources.quote: one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA

risks: BACnet/IP is not evidenced in Kiss's supplied publications or project summaries; the closest protocol-agnostic work was evaluated on other protocols, so transfer to BACnet must be tested in the first experiment.
Kiss's availability is unknown; no source in the material confirms her capacity, which could delay a joint project.
Evaluation without real labelled attacks depends on injected or replayed anomalies and held-out normal captures; these may not represent stealthy or unknown attacks.
Site-specific baselines may drift with seasonal load and process changes; recalibration schedules validated on testbeds need revalidation on ArmaturaSec's multi-site archives.
Client traffic is sensitive and shared under consent and NDA; data-sharing and privacy constraints could limit access to BACnet and multi-site captures.
ArmaturaSec's previous supervised classifier caused alert fatigue; a new unsupervised detector could fail the same operational acceptance test if false alarms are not calibrated.
questions: Does Krisztina Kiss have the availability and supervisory capacity for a joint project in the coming academic year, and can her group's testbed data-sharing agreement be applied to ArmaturaSec?
Which ArmaturaSec traffic archives and BACnet/IP captures can be shared under NDA, for which sites and time periods, and do they include any known incidents or operator annotations?
What target hardware and resource budget should the first prototype meet: existing ProtoSense/NetGuard appliances or the planned late-2025 security-processor variant?
What false-positive rate, alert volume and explanation format would be acceptable to ArmaturaSec's clients and plant managers?
Can controlled anomalies be injected on a testbed or mirrored network for evaluation, and what ethical, customer-consent or regulatory approvals are needed?
Should the first experiment prioritise Modbus TCP, where Kiss has direct evidence, or BACnet/IP, where ArmaturaSec needs coverage but the researcher's material shows a gap?
How will jointly developed detector code and models be licensed and integrated into ArmaturaSec's proprietary firmware?
